title: 1. Say it with print
summary: The first program: making Python show text and numbers.

steps.title: Say hello
steps.instructions: Use print() to show the greeting below, exactly as written.

steps.title: Two lines
steps.instructions: Each print() starts a new line. Print the two lines below with two print() calls.

steps.title: Let Python do the sum
steps.instructions: print() can show the result of a calculation. Print the result of 2 + 3 without typing the answer yourself.

steps.title: Words and a number together
steps.instructions: Give print() several things separated by commas and it puts a space between them. Print the sentence below using the text "I am", the number 12 and the text "years old".

title: 2. Variables
summary: Giving a value a name, using it, and changing it.

steps.title: Store a name
steps.instructions: Make a variable called name that holds the text "Asha". Then print the variable.

steps.title: Use it in a sentence
steps.instructions: Keep the variable name from the last step. Print a greeting that uses it, so the output is the line below.

steps.title: Numbers in variables
steps.instructions: Make price = 40 and count = 3. Print the total cost, which is price times count. Use * to multiply.

steps.title: Change a variable
steps.instructions: Start with score = 10. Add 5 to score, then print score.

title: 3. Asking with input
summary: Reading what the user types and answering with it.

steps.title: Repeat what was typed
steps.instructions: input() waits for a line of text and gives it back. Read one line into a variable and print it.

steps.title: Greet by name
steps.instructions: Read a name with input(). Print a greeting for that name, ending with an exclamation mark, like the line below. Do not put a question inside input() for this step, because that text would be printed too.

steps.title: Two answers
steps.instructions: Read a city, then a country, with two input() calls. Print them on one line with a comma and a space between them.

title: 4. Numbers and sums
summary: Turning typed text into numbers and calculating with them.

steps.title: Add two numbers
steps.instructions: input() always gives text. Wrap it in int() to get a whole number. Read two whole numbers and print their sum.

steps.title: Area of a rectangle
steps.instructions: Read the width, then the height, as whole numbers. Print the area, which is width times height.

steps.title: Average of three
steps.instructions: Read three whole numbers. Print their average: add them and divide by 3 with /. Dividing with / always gives a decimal number, so 7 shows as 7.0.

steps.title: What is left over
steps.instructions: The % sign gives the remainder of a division. Read a whole number and print the remainder when it is divided by 2.

title: 5. Choosing with if and else
summary: Making the program do one thing or another.

steps.title: Pass or fail
steps.instructions: Read marks as a whole number. If the marks are 40 or more print Pass, otherwise print Fail. Use >= for "or more".

steps.title: The other side
steps.instructions: Do not change your program. Check it again here, where the marks are 20. A program that only ever prints Pass will not get through this step.

steps.title: Even or odd
steps.instructions: Read a whole number. Print Even if it divides by 2 with nothing left over, otherwise print Odd. The remainder sign % from the last lesson helps.

steps.title: The bigger one
steps.instructions: Read two whole numbers. Print the bigger of the two.

title: 6. More than two choices
summary: Using elif when there are several cases.

steps.title: A grade for the marks
steps.instructions: Read marks as a whole number and print a grade: A for 80 or more, B for 60 or more, C for 40 or more, and F for anything lower. Use if, then elif for each next case, then else.

steps.title: The same program, other marks
steps.instructions: Do not change your program. This time the marks are 65.

steps.title: And the lowest grade
steps.instructions: Still the same program. This time the marks are 10.

steps.title: Positive, negative or zero
steps.instructions: Read a whole number. Print Positive if it is more than 0, Negative if it is less than 0, and Zero if it is 0.

title: 7. Repeating with for
summary: Doing something a set number of times with for and range.

steps.title: Count to five
steps.instructions: Print the numbers 1 to 5, one on each line, using a for loop. range(1, 6) gives the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: it stops before 6.

steps.title: Count as far as asked
steps.instructions: Read a whole number n. Print the numbers from 1 to n, one on each line.

steps.title: A times table
steps.instructions: Read a whole number. Print the first five lines of its times table, in the form shown below.

steps.title: Add them all up
steps.instructions: Read a whole number n. Print the sum of all the numbers from 1 to n. Start a total at 0 and add to it inside the loop.

title: 8. Repeating with while
summary: Repeating for as long as something stays true.

steps.title: Countdown
steps.instructions: Start a variable at 5. While it is more than 0, print it and take 1 away. After the loop, print Go!

steps.title: Keep halving
steps.instructions: Read a whole number. While it is more than 0, print it and then halve it with //, which divides and drops the part after the decimal point.

steps.title: Add until zero
steps.instructions: Keep reading whole numbers and adding them to a total. Stop when the number read is 0, then print the total.

title: 9. Lists
summary: Keeping several values together and going through them.

steps.title: Make a list and show it
steps.instructions: Make a list called fruits holding "apple", "banana" and "mango". Print each fruit on its own line with a for loop.

steps.title: How many
steps.instructions: Keep the list from the last step. Print how many fruits are in it, using len().

steps.title: Add one more
steps.instructions: Keep the list. Add "orange" to the end with fruits.append("orange"). Then print the last fruit, which is fruits[-1], and on the next line how many fruits there are now.

steps.title: The biggest number
steps.instructions: Make a list called numbers holding 4, 17, 9 and 2. Print the biggest number in it. You can go through the list remembering the biggest so far, or use max().

title: 10. Functions
summary: Giving a piece of code a name so it can be used again.

steps.title: A function that greets
steps.instructions: Define a function greet(name) that prints a greeting for the name, in the form shown below. Call it twice: once with "Asha" and once with "Bikram".

steps.title: A function that gives back a value
steps.instructions: Define a function square(n) that returns n times n. It should not print anything itself. Print square(4), then print square(9).

steps.title: Use it with input
steps.instructions: Keep your square function. Read a whole number and print its square by calling the function.

steps.title: True or False
steps.instructions: Define a function is_even(n) that returns True when n is even and False when it is not. Print is_even(10), then print is_even(7).
